subject.title: Prompt-cache prefix churn on OpenAI models: per-turn dynamic injections (message tool hint + volatile system-prompt section) defeat automatic prefix caching

question: Should OpenAI/Codex visible-reply guidance be moved into current-turn content while keeping `message` tool schemas stable, or should maintainers choose a broader prompt-assembly/cache-boundary contract first?
rationale: The source-backed bug is real, but the durable fix crosses source-channel delivery semantics, OpenAI prefix-cache behavior, and current docs, so automation should not pick the permanent contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Move guidance turn-local
options.body: Keep the `message` tool schema stable and carry `message_tool_only` instructions in current-turn user/runtime content for OpenAI-family requests, with delivery and cache proof.

options.title: Design broader cache contract
options.body: Pause the narrow fix until maintainers define one provider-wide prompt assembly contract for all volatile runtime sections and tool metadata.

options.title: Document limitation only
options.body: Update prompt-caching docs to warn that OpenAI automatic prefix caching still loses reuse when delivery-mode bytes change, without changing runtime behavior yet.

recommendation.title: Move guidance turn-local
recommendation.body: Keep the `message` tool schema stable and carry `message_tool_only` instructions in current-turn user/runtime content for OpenAI-family requests, with delivery and cache proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest prompt-cache boundary and transport history among the identified routing candidates.
